overview: Democrats have secured a historic House majority by clinching 258 seats, while international climate talks at COP31 in Turkey collapsed after countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuel phase-outs. In national business news, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia to provide answers regarding chip sales to China. Locally in San Francisco, city officials are considering moving a courthouse downtown due to seismic concerns at the Hall of Justice. Meanwhile, Hawaii news features ongoing scrutiny over the state's homeless policy and kauhale tiny house initiatives following a critical assessment by the state auditor.

items.title: Democrats Clinch 258 House Seats, an Election-Year Record This Century
items.summary: After sweeping midterm wins, Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a national election for either party in three decades.

items.title: COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
items.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey collapsed after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels.

items.title: Scott Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia to provide answers regarding its chip sales to China.

items.title: Mall of Justice? Supes eye moving courthouse downtown
items.summary: San Francisco supervisors are evaluating a proposal to move a courthouse downtown because the Hall of Justice on Bryant Street is seismically unsound.

items.title: Neal Milner: Green Should Idle His Indignation Machine, Look Hard At Kauhale
items.summary: A columnist examines the state's homeless policy and Gov. Josh Green's kauhale tiny house initiative following a critical assessment by the state auditor.

wiki.title: Mairzy Doates
wiki.extract: Mairzy Doates was an American Thoroughbred racehorse and multiple graded stakes winner, most remembered for her victory at the inaugural Japan Cup in 1981. Owned by New York City art dealer Arno D. Schefler and trained primarily by future U.S. Racing Hall of Fame inductee Horatio Luro, she competed successfully across the United States from 1978 to 1981, including winning the Yerba Buena Handicap twice.
